title: Chain of Custody: Automation & Evidence Packaging Spec
content:
Purpose:
This document defines an implementation specification for automated chain-of-custody packaging and signing of control evidence produced by Redwood inference platform components. The goal is to standardize how evidence is collected, normalized, signed, and exported (to archive and SIEM) so audits and control reviews can deterministically reconstruct events and attestations without manual assembly.

Scope:
- Applies to automated evidence produced by: RBAC v2 changes, audit-log ingestion pipeline, control-evidence collectors (agents running on hosted/dedicated/private), SIEM export adapters, and evidence-backfill jobs.
- Out of scope: manual compliance artifacts produced outside the platform (e.g., customer-supplied third-party attestations).

Background and motivation:
- Current evidence is fragmented across: raw audit events, periodic snapshots, attestations from services, and SIEM exports. Auditors want a single reproducible "bundle" for each control evaluation and a verifiable chain of custody.
- This spec introduces an evidence packaging pipeline that:
  * Normalizes diverse event sources into a common audit schema;
  * Produces signed, timebound evidence bundles with metadata and provenance;
  * Integrates RBAC v2 decision records and policy snapshots as first-class evidence;
  * Supports streaming SIEM export as well as archive exports for long-term retention.

Goals and success criteria:
- End-to-end automated bundle generation for control evaluations with >95% completeness for required evidence fields.
- Deterministic bundle identifiers so reruns/backfills reference the same evidence artifact when input data is unchanged.
- Cryptographically signed bundles (platform KMS-backed key) with verification utilities.
- Minimal runtime overhead on production paths (target: <3% p95 latency overhead for synchronous control checks).

High-level architecture:
- Ingest layer: Collectors (lightweight agents or sidecar pipelines) push raw events to a normalized event bus (Kafka or equivalent).
- Normalizer: Stateless service that maps source-specific fields into the canonical audit schema, enriches with identity metadata (RBAC v2 principal IDs), and tags with control mapping.
- Assembler: Stateful service that collects events for a control evaluation window, deduplicates, orders events, and assembles an evidence manifest.
- Signer & Notary: Attaches signatures/timestamps using KMS-managed keys, emits verification metadata.
- Exporter: Two sinks: (1) SIEM adapter for near-real-time export (configurable filters and batching); (2) Evidence archive (object storage, immutable write-once paths).
- API & CLI: Retrieval, verification, and rehydrate endpoints for auditors and internal tooling.

Canonical audit schema (summary):
- NOTE: full schema in appendix. Listed fields are required by evidence assembler.
  - event_id: string (uuid v4)
  - timestamp_utc: string (RFC3339)
  - source_service: string (serving-runtime | dedicated-orchestrator | console)
  - event_type: string (authz_decision | policy_change | model_deploy | config_change | request_trace | error)
  - principal_id: string (rbac v2 subject id)
  - principal_type: string (human | service | api_key)
  - decision: string (allow | deny | no_decision) -- optional for non-auth events
  - resource_type: string
  - resource_id: string
  - request_id: string -- correlates to trace ids where available
  - payload: string (base64-encoded compressed JSON) -- raw event body for forensic needs
  - control_tags: list<string> (e.g., C-ACCESS-001, C-DEPLOY-003)
  - retention_tier: string (audit-short | audit-long | pii-protected)
  - ingest_path: string (collector-id / stream partition)

RBAC v2 interaction and evidence capture:
- Whenever a policy change is applied to RBAC v2 (role update, policy attach/detach, schema migration):
  * Emit a policy_change event with fields: change_id, author, diff_patch (unified diff), policy_version_after.
  * Snapshot the effective policy set at time T and include snapshot reference in the bundle.
- For authorization decisions relevant to controls (e.g., elevated ops actions, data access to pii-protected resources):
  * Emit authz_decision events including a deterministic decision_signature computed from principal_id, resource_id, action, and timestamp.

Evidence bundle format and metadata (assembler outputs):
- bundle_id: deterministic sha256 over ordered event_ids + assembler_version + assembly_window_start; represented as hex string.
- bundle_version: semver string for assembler code version.
- assembly_window: start_ts, end_ts (RFC3339).
- included_event_count: integer as string.
- manifest: newline-delimited list of event_id -> s3/object-path or kafka-offset.
- provenance: list of source_signatures (service-id, signature, signature_alg, key_id).
- verification: verification_url (API endpoint), verification_hash (sha256 of signed bundle file).
- control_map: list of control_ids covered and rationale mapping (short form text).
- custody_log: ordered actions (collected, normalized, assembled, signed, exported) with timestamps and actor ids.

Signing model and KMS integration:
- Use platform KMS with dedicated signing keys per environment (dev/stage/prod) and per-tenant key wrappers for private installs.
- Keys are rotated quarterly; bundles must include key_id and rotation_epoch.
- Signer produces detached signature files and an embedded signature in the bundle manifest for quick checks.

SIEM export adapter rules and flow:
- Exporter receives assembler deltas and manifests. SIEM adapter maps canonical audit schema to SIEM event model (ids, severity, category).
- Configurable exporter rules: filter_by_control_tag, suppress_pii (redaction rules), batch_window_ms, backpressure_strategy (drop | block | spill-to-archive).
- For high-volume events (request_trace), exporter only ships event summary + reference to archive path; full payload remains in archive.

Retention and legal hold:
- Evidence archive supports retention tiers with policy enforcement:
  * audit-short: 1 year
  * audit-long: 7 years
  * pii-protected: configurable per-customer; default 7 years
- Legal hold supersedes retention; a legal-hold flag on a bundle prevents deletion and triggers extended monitoring.

Backfill & idempotency rules:
- Assembler must support idempotent replays: if the same ordered set of event_ids is provided, bundle_id must be identical.
- Backfill jobs annotate bundle.metadata.backfill=true and include original_ingest_window.
- For events with missing payloads, assembler emits evidence_gap markers and a gap_resolution_ticket id so auditors can trace remediation.

Observability and SLOs:
- Metrics: bundle_assembly_latency_p50/p95, assembler_errors_total, signer_failures, export_rate, siem_export_latency.
- Traces: end-to-end trace ids must include collector->normalizer->assembler->signer->exporter spans.
- SLO: 99% of control evidence bundles for synchronous controls must be available within 2 minutes of end of assembly window.

Operational playbooks (short):
- Missing signer keys: fail-safe to write unsigned bundles flagged untrusted and send pager to secops; do NOT drop the evidence.
- Exporter backpressure: if SIEM export blocks, spill bundles to archive and mark export_status=deferred.
- Evidence gaps: create backfill ticket and attach gap_resolution_ticket to bundle manifest.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests for normalizer mappings and schema validation.
- Integration tests simulating RBAC v2 policy rollout and a set of authz_decision events to verify deterministic bundle_id.
- Cryptographic verification tests that attempt signature verification using public keys from KMS.
- End-to-end rehearsal: monthly rehearsals that create an ephemeral bundle, verify, and then delete. Rehearsal results stored in a short-lived namespace.

Migration notes (from current fragmentation):
- Phase 1: Pilot for one control family (C-ACCESS-001): deploy collectors, normalizer, assembler in a staging environment; capture both existing artifacts and new bundles in parallel for 30 days.
- Phase 2: Expand to additional controls and enable SIEM export adapter in dry-run; compare with existing SIEM ingestion.
- Phase 3: Cutover, route downstream consumers to bundle verification API and deprecate legacy artifact assembly scripts.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do we include full raw payloads in SIEM exports for PII-sensitive events, or always reference archive? Recommendation: reference archive and only export summaries for pii_protected events.
- What is acceptable bundle size limit? Suggest 200MB compressed and export policy to archive multipart bundles beyond that.
- Per-tenant key management in Redwood Private: allow customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed key.

Appendix (examples):
- Example manifest excerpt:
  {
    "bundle_id": "b3f6c3...",
    "assembly_window": {"start": "2025-05-28T12:00:00Z", "end": "2025-05-28T12:05:00Z"},
    "events": ["e8a9d2...", "f03c11..."],
    "provenance": [{"service": "rbac-service", "signature": "MEUCIQ...", "key_id": "kms-prod-keys/keys/ck-2025-01"}]
  }

- Example audit event (canonical):
  {
    "event_id": "e8a9d21f-7d1a-4c5e-9a6e-1b2c3d4f5a6b",
    "timestamp_utc": "2025-05-28T12:00:01Z",
    "source_service": "rbac-service",
    "event_type": "policy_change",
    "principal_id": "user:ashap",
    "principal_type": "human",
    "payload": "H4sIAAAAA...base64 gzipped diff...",
    "control_tags": ["C-ACCESS-001"],
    "retention_tier": "audit-long"
  }

Contact and next steps:
- Owner: Asha Patel (security engineer)
- Immediate next steps: schedule architecture review with observability and infra (Evan Coleman, Nadia Kaur), confirm signer KMS policy, build prototype assembler job for C-ACCESS-001 pilot by 2025-02-15.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally conservative on including payloads; we should validate PII redaction rules with privacy/legal.
- Want feedback on deterministic bundle_id algorithm if there are objections to including assembler_version in the hash.
